title: Measurement of Bioelectric Current with a Vibrating Probe
protocol: Probe manufacture is not described in the given protocol, so no steps can be provided for this task based on the information available.
However, if there were details about probe manufacturing, each step related to it would follow the format specified:
- Begin with a verb.
- Include precise instructions and reagent volumes when applicable.
- Exclude irrelevant or non-experimental content.
Cut the probe 25-30 mm behind the tip.
Scrape away about 5 mm of parylene insulation at the cut end with a scalpel (#11 blade).
Mount the probe in a gold R30 connector using electrically-conductive silver-loaded epoxy.
Store the probe overnight at room temperature to allow the epoxy to harden.

Plate the probe tip with gold using a nano-amp power supply and gold plating solution (potassium dicyanoaurate) for 5 min at 5 nA, then increase current until the tip is about half the desired final size.
Rinse the probe tip in distilled water (dH2O).

Place the probe tip in platinizing solution (chloroplatinic acid hydrate plus lead(II) acetate trihydrate) and apply a current of 500 nA for several minutes until the tip reaches about 80% of the desired final size.
Increase current to 1 μA and apply in 1 sec bursts until final tip diameter is obtained (about 30-35 μm).
Rinse the tip in dH2O.
Attach the probe to a piezo-electric bender.
Mount the piezo-electric bender on a 3-dimensional micro-positioner.
Adjust the vibration amplitude and frequency using the vibrating probe power supply.
Send a reference signal from the probe power supply to the lock-in amplifier.
Display the vibration frequency and phase angle on the lock-in amplifier.
Connect an oscilloscope for visual monitoring of probe vibration.
Route the signal from the probe to the lock-in amplifier.
View the probe and sample under a dissecting microscope with fiber-optic illumination (magnification x6 to x40).
Place a reference and ground wire in the solution during calibration and measurements.
Connect the amplifier to a computer via an analog-digital interface.
Record data using Strathclyde Electrophysiology Software's Whole Cell Program (WinWCP).
Set sensitivity to 200 μV in the lock-in amplifier.
Set dynamic resolution to normal in the lock-in amplifier.
Turn on offset control in the lock-in amplifier.
Set expand mode to x1 in the lock-in amplifier.
Set pre Time Constant to 10 s in the lock-in amplifier.
Set post Time Constant to 0.1 s in the lock-in amplifier.
Adjust pre Time Constant to 3 s if a faster response is required.
Move the probe trace near the center of the screen using offset control.
Increase voltage range to 1 V or 5 V in WCP software if large currents are anticipated.
Set record duration to 204.8 s in WCP software.
Set samples per channel to 1024 in WCP software.
Set sampling interval to 0.2 s in WCP software.
Set voltage range to +/- 0.2 V in WCP software.
Place new probes in a calibration chamber containing physiological saline.
Turn on the power supply and adjust the frequency until maximum vibration is observed.
Subtract 10 Hz from the resonant frequency to determine the working frequency (typically 150-200 Hz).
Adjust the vibration amplitude so that the probe's vibration distance equals its tip diameter, creating a 'double image' of the probe tip.
Apply a current of 1.5 μA/cm² repeatedly while adjusting the phase angle until there is no response on the lock-in amplifier.
Add or subtract 90° to find the maximum response and set this as the working phase angle for the probe.
Note the frequency and phase angle settings for each probe for future use.
Maintain the same settings of frequency, amplitude, and phase angle during experiments.
Calibrate the probe in an appropriate solution, such as BSS+ Artificial Tear Solution for cornea, prior to sample measurement.
Apply a standardized current of exactly 1.5 μA/cm² to the probe in a calibration chamber to determine the response.
Calibrate the probe again at the end of the experiment using the used solution to compensate for osmolality changes due to evaporation.
Measure the current in the sample by applying it in two directions: South-North and North-South, producing upward and downward deflections respectively.
Place the dish containing physiological saline under the dissecting microscope.
Focus on the area of interest on the sample in the field of view.
Orientate the probe parallel to the sample surface and place it in focus.
Move the probe away from the sample to establish a stable baseline.
Position the probe about 50 μm from the surface for measurement.
Stabilize the new value when measuring and return the probe to reference position.
Repeat measurements at regular time points for timelapse data.
Rotate or move the sample slightly for spatial current mapping data.
Move the red line up until it is parallel with the top of the peak.
Record the green output reading as the size of the peak in mV.
Enter data for all measurement peaks and calibration data into a Microsoft Excel spreadsheet template.
Note relevant information such as date, probe number, voltage range (VR), solution used, measuring positions, time-points in the spreadsheet.
Note current direction into or out of the sample ('i/o') in the spreadsheet.
Assign negative values to inward currents in the 'peak' column.
Calculate the current using the formula: current = peak * (1.5 / calibration).
Earthy the micro-positioner.
Earth the chassis of the microscope.
Earth the light source if necessary.
Use a wrist-band to earth the user if needed.
Filter out frequencies using a lock-in amplifier.
Utilize a vibration isolation table if available.
Record changes in temperature in the lab-book.
Document drug additions in the lab-book.
Note magnification when taking photographs under the microscope.
Draw sketches of samples showing probe measurement positions and orientations.
Use appropriate saline or culture medium for the sample you will measure.
Ensure the liquid surface is flat across the top of the calibration chamber.
Plan and create special chambers if necessary to hold or mount samples.
Orientate the probe with its long axis parallel to the sample surface.
Maintain a consistent distance between the probe and the sample surface during measurements.
Use an eyepiece graticule to judge the distance between the probe and the sample surface.
Check that saline contacts both electrodes when there is no response at calibration.
Verify the battery in the constant current calibrator when troubleshooting no response.
Clean probe in dH2O and/or acetone.
Check phase angle.
Check earthing wires.
Do not allow probe tip to touch sample.
